nodes.label: G1: feePaise Always Zero Invariant
nodes.rationale: Enforces a zero booking/convenience-fee guarantee across every payment and booking record; chosen as a hard global constraint so no task can silently introduce a fee, verified by a test on every charge-path change.

nodes.label: G2: Quote Token Validation Gate
nodes.rationale: Code-level enforcement of 'first price = final price' -- a signed token carrying legId+price must validate before any charge, preventing client-side price tampering between quote and payment.

nodes.label: backend/ Monolith Retirement
nodes.rationale: The monolith was retired because the microservices split was confirmed strictly ahead of it (every controller superseded or exceeded) and it was unreferenced by CI, docker-compose, and the frontend -- a large, hard-to-reverse deletion gated behind explicit user confirmation.

nodes.label: Payment-Gated Confirmation
nodes.rationale: A leg/booking must be confirmed only after a verified CAPTURED webhook, never on order creation or an unverified client-side signal, closing the always-succeeds sandbox gap.

nodes.label: Webhook Idempotency (processed_webhook_events)
nodes.rationale: A re-delivered payment.captured webhook must be a no-op rather than a double-capture/double-publish; implemented first as a Firestore dedupe collection keyed by provider payment id.

nodes.label: A2 Fail-Fast Secret Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every new secret is an env var with no in-source default, and the owning bean fails fast via @PostConstruct on a blank/short value -- prevents a silently-broken signature check running on a placeholder secret.

nodes.label: A3 Per-Service Secret Scoping
nodes.rationale: Each secret/env var is emitted only to the services that actually consume it via per-service case blocks in backend-deploy.yml, replacing an earlier pattern that sprayed every secret to every service.

nodes.label: P1.2 IDOR / Ownership Enforcement Fix
nodes.rationale: Closes an IDOR on payment-service's getStatus by capturing ownerUserId at write time and enforcing it on reads (with a ROLE_ADMIN bypass), the first such bypass pattern in the codebase.

nodes.label: PENDING to CONFIRMED Leg/Booking State Machine
nodes.rationale: Booking/Leg must never be set CONFIRMED at creation time -- confirmation happens only in the payment.captured consumers, closing the premature-confirmation bug found in both booking-service and trip-service.
nodes.norm_label: pending to confirmed leg/booking state machine

nodes.label: F2: circuitBreakers Readiness Boot Bug
nodes.rationale: trip-service crashed at boot because management.health.circuitbreakers.enabled was never set, so referencing circuitBreakers in the readiness group threw NoSuchHealthContributorException -- a real bug that reached main undetected because no CI test gate existed.

nodes.label: F1: CI Test Gate
nodes.rationale: Standardizes every service's context-load test to disable Firestore/GCP auto-config and mock repositories so 'mvnw clean verify' needs zero real infrastructure, then wires a PR-triggered workflow across all 9 services to catch regressions like F2 before they reach main.

nodes.label: P1.3 Firestore to Postgres Money Ledger Migration
nodes.rationale: Moves Payment and ProcessedWebhookEvent off Firestore onto Cloud SQL Postgres so the webhook-capture race can be closed with a DB-enforced atomic transaction instead of Firestore's check-then-act pattern.
nodes.norm_label: p1.3 firestore to postgres money ledger migration

nodes.label: Atomic Webhook-Capture Transaction
nodes.rationale: Replaces the Firestore check-then-act dedupe with one @Transactional method: insert-into-dedupe-or-noop then a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='CREATED', closing the concurrent-webhook-delivery race that could double-capture.

nodes.label: Transactional Outbox Pattern
nodes.rationale: Writes payment.captured/refunded as a durable outbox row in the same DB transaction as the state change, with a scheduled relay as the sole publisher, so a crash between commit and publish no longer loses the event.

nodes.label: DLQ + Bounded Retry Consumer Hardening
nodes.rationale: Removes the top-level swallow-everything try/catch in both payment.captured consumers so an unrecoverable message retries with backoff then dead-letters instead of being silently dropped.

nodes.label: leg.confirmed Single-Owner Choreography
nodes.rationale: Moves confirmation ownership so trip-service alone confirms Leg off payment.captured and emits leg.confirmed, which booking-service re-binds to instead of consuming payment.captured directly -- so Booking can never diverge from Leg's confirmation state.

nodes.label: Java 25 LTS Runtime Upgrade Goal
nodes.rationale: User-requested latest LTS runtime upgrade (17 to 25) with Spring Boot/Spring Cloud/dependency versions held unchanged unless compilation proves an incompatibility -- deliberately scoped to avoid unrelated API migration.

nodes.label: A4: Per-Service Dedicated Service Accounts
nodes.rationale: Replaces the shared default compute SA with one dedicated least-privilege SA per Cloud Run service plus per-caller run.invoker bindings, closing the gap where 'any Cloud Run workload in the project' could call an internal-only service.

nodes.label: Server-Side Quote Token Signing
nodes.rationale: QuoteTokenService.issue was implemented in Phase 0 but never actually called from application code, so bookLeg's validation could never pass for a real caller; this fix signs the token immediately after the Leg is first saved and always overwrites any client-supplied token.

nodes.label: Gateway Payment Routes (order/status/refund)
nodes.rationale: api-gateway only routed the webhook path to payment-service; order/status/refund calls were not gateway-routed at all, making the payment flow unreachable from a real browser -- a new routes[10] entry closes this.

nodes.label: Leg-Booking Confirmation Email
nodes.rationale: LegConfirmedConsumer only logged a TODO instead of notifying; closed by adding email/phone fields sourced from the frontend JWT (no backend user-lookup) and a plain-text EmailService.sendLegBookingConfirmation path.

nodes.label: Firestore-Emulator Test Pattern (rejected)
nodes.rationale: identity-service's existing context-load test expected a real Firestore emulator process on localhost:8080 that nothing in the repo starts -- confirmed broken on main, and rejected as the standard pattern in favor of disable-GCP + mock-repos.

nodes.label: Disable-GCP + Mock-Repos Test Pattern
nodes.rationale: Standardized across all 9 services because it needs no real infrastructure or credentials and was already proven working by booking-service/trip-service/payment-service, unlike the ambient-ADC-dependent or emulator-dependent alternatives.
